questions.question_text: What is the minimum age to obtain a NH real estate salesperson license?
questions.explanation: New Hampshire requires salesperson applicants to be at least 18 years of age. This is consistent with the legal age to enter into binding contracts in the state.

questions.question_text: How many hours of pre-license education must a NH salesperson candidate complete?
questions.explanation: NH requires 40 hours of approved pre-license study for salesperson candidates (RSA 331-A:10, I(b)). Under Rea 301.03(q), at least 32 of those hours must be classroom attendance or real-time internet live-class instruction; self-paced distance education is limited to 8 hours and is allowed only to make up acceptable absences such as illness or a family emergency.

questions.question_text: A candidate wants to complete all 40 pre-license hours online. Is this permitted in NH?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, if the hours are live, real-time online classes
distractors: No, at least 32 hours must be in a physical classroom
No, all 40 hours must be completed in person
Yes, including fully self-paced recorded courses
questions.explanation: Rea 301.03(q) treats real-time internet live-class instruction - live video and audio of all participants with instructor monitoring - the same as classroom attendance. A candidate may therefore complete all 40 hours online if at least 32 hours are live-class instruction. Self-paced distance education (recordings or correspondence with a final exam) is capped at 8 hours and is allowed only to make up acceptable absences such as illness, family emergency, or technical problems during a live class.

questions.question_text: Within what time frame must a candidate complete pre-license education before taking the state exam?
questions.explanation: NH requires the 40-hour pre-license course to be begun and completed within the 6 months before the licensing exam (Rea 301.03(q); PSI Candidate Handbook). Candidates outside this window must retake the course before testing, and a candidate who tests without valid education must retake the entire exam even after passing (Rea 301.03(r)).

questions.question_text: A candidate completed pre-license education 8 months ago and now wants to take the exam. What must the candidate do?
questions.explanation: Pre-license education must be begun and completed within the 6 months before the licensing exam (Rea 301.03(q); PSI Candidate Handbook). A candidate whose course was completed 8 months prior has exceeded the validity window and must retake the entire 40-hour pre-license course.

questions.question_text: What criminal background check is required for NH licensure?
questions.explanation: NH requires a criminal records check through the NH State Police as a condition of licensure. The results of this check are valid for 6 months from the date of issuance.

questions.question_text: A candidate obtained a criminal records check 7 months ago. Can she use this for her license application?
questions.correct_answer: No, the check is only valid for 6 months
distractors: Yes, it is valid for 12 months
Yes, there is no expiration date
No, she needs a federal check instead
questions.explanation: The NH State Police criminal records check is valid for only 6 months. After that period, the applicant must obtain a new records check to submit with the license application.

questions.question_text: A candidate passes the national portion of the NH exam but fails the state portion. What happens next?
questions.correct_answer: The candidate must retake the state portion
distractors: The candidate receives a full license
Both portions must be retaken together
questions.explanation: The NH licensing exam is split — candidates must pass both the national and state portions independently at 70%. If only one portion is failed, the candidate retakes only that portion within the allowed timeframe.

questions.question_text: A candidate scores 75% on the national portion but 65% on the state portion. What is the result?
questions.correct_answer: Only the state portion must be retaken
distractors: The candidate passes the exam overall
Both portions must be retaken together
The scores are averaged to reach 70%
questions.explanation: Each portion is scored independently: 56/80 (70%) on the national portion and 28/40 (70%) on the state portion are required. Having passed the national portion, the candidate keeps that credit and, under Rea 303.05(a), reschedules and pays a new exam fee to retake only the failed state portion. Both portions must be passed within 6 months of the original exam date (Rea 303.05(b)), or the candidate must retake the pre-licensing course and the entire exam.

questions.question_text: A candidate has failed the NH licensing exam multiple times. What does NH require before allowing additional attempts?
questions.correct_answer: Retake the pre-license course after repeated failures
distractors: There is no limit on exam attempts in NH
The candidate must wait one year to retake
The candidate must obtain a waiver from OPLC
questions.explanation: After 8 examination attempts - or if both portions are not passed within 6 months of the original exam date - the candidate must complete an accredited pre-licensing course again (in addition to the original course) and retake the entire examination (Rea 303.05(b)).

questions.question_text: What is the NH real estate license renewal cycle?
questions.explanation: New Hampshire real estate licenses are valid for 2 years from issuance (RSA 310:8, II). Renewal fees are set through OPLC: $90 for salespersons and $110 for brokers. Active licensees must also complete 15 hours of continuing education each renewal period.

questions.question_text: How many continuing education hours are required per renewal period in NH?
questions.explanation: NH licensees must complete 15 hours of continuing education each biennial renewal period. This includes 3 hours of mandatory core topics and 12 hours of electives for active licensees; an inactive licensee renewing on inactive status needs only the 3-hour core course.

questions.question_text: A licensee completes 12 elective CE hours but skips the core requirement. Can the license be renewed?
questions.explanation: The 15-hour CE requirement includes 3 mandatory core hours that cannot be replaced by elective hours. Both the 3 core hours and 12 elective hours must be completed for a valid renewal.

questions.question_text: What additional CE requirement applies to a licensee renewing for the first time?
questions.explanation: For a salesperson's first renewal, the 12 elective hours must be satisfied with commission-designated post-licensing courses, taken along with the 3-hour core course (Rea 403.01(c)-(d); RSA 331-A:25, IX). The post-licensing topics replace the ordinary electives rather than adding hours - the total remains 15.

questions.question_text: A licensed broker from Vermont wants to practice in NH. Under HB 594, what reciprocity does NH offer?
questions.explanation: OPLC licenses applicants holding an active license in good standing from any jurisdiction with substantially similar requirements — a path created by HB 594 (2023) as RSA 310:17 — and the PSI handbook confirms NH has reciprocity with all 50 states. Under the real-estate recognition statute, RSA 331-A:11-a, an out-of-state licensee who qualified by passing national and state exams obtains the equivalent NH license by passing the New Hampshire portion of the licensing exam.
